purpose: Structured retrieval registry for BeSci dimensions, processes, computational axes, higher-order factors, and interpretive principles.

corpus_families.name: affective_language_and_psycholinguistics
corpus_families.interpretive_use: Grounds direct emotional language, negative style, self-focus, and language-based mental health approximations.

corpus_families.name: computational_psychiatry_and_process_models
corpus_families.interpretive_use: Explains how reward, effort, uncertainty, and control may shape language over time.

corpus_families.name: reward_motivation_and_anhedonia
corpus_families.interpretive_use: Distinguishes low reward pull, effort burden, and activation from general sadness.

corpus_families.name: social_relational_and_rdco_social_constructs
corpus_families.interpretive_use: Keeps social life multi-dimensional and allows performance, attachment, evaluation, and intimacy to vary independently.

corpus_families.name: dimensional_hierarchy_and_symptom_covariance
corpus_families.interpretive_use: Summarizes covariance patterns without forcing categorical diagnosis.

corpus_families.name: trajectory_and_longitudinal_epidemiology
corpus_families.interpretive_use: Constrains how same-day, short-horizon, and longer-horizon changes are interpreted.

corpus_families.name: expressive_poetic_and_aesthetic_corpora
corpus_families.interpretive_use: Allows BeSci to treat figurative, image-rich, and symbolic language as meaningful rather than as low-information noise.

dimensions.name: valence
dimensions.meaning: Overall emotional tone from more distressed or empty to more supported or positively toned.
dimensions.llm_rule: Do not equate valence with diagnosis. Combine with reward, arousal, and domain context before summarizing.

dimensions.name: arousal
dimensions.meaning: Level of activation, urgency, vigilance, or embodied calm.
dimensions.llm_rule: Use time-scale context. Same-day spikes may reflect event load, fatigue, or circadian movement rather than durable worsening.

dimensions.name: control
dimensions.meaning: Felt organization, follow-through, and self-regulatory steadiness.
dimensions.llm_rule: Interpret with control_allocation and effort_cost_load when possible.

dimensions.name: volatility
dimensions.meaning: Expectation or expression of instability, abrupt shifts, and uncertainty-driven movement.
dimensions.llm_rule: Do not confuse volatility with intensity alone. It is about instability and unpredictability.

dimensions.name: social_orientation
dimensions.meaning: How connected, withdrawn, socially active, or interpersonally pulled back the language sounds.
dimensions.llm_rule: Do not flatten this into one good/bad social score when relational ambivalence or evaluative concern are also high.

dimensions.name: reward_seeking
dimensions.meaning: Interest, pull, curiosity, reward sensitivity, and motivational availability.
dimensions.llm_rule: Keep this distinct from valence. Low reward can coexist with partial functioning or even mixed tone.

dimensions.name: cognitive_flexibility
dimensions.meaning: Capacity for reframing, adjusting, and moving out of rigid cognitive loops.

dimensions.name: self_focus
dimensions.meaning: Degree of inward self-reference and self-directed attention.
dimensions.llm_rule: Self-focus is not automatically pathological; its meaning depends on valence, flexibility, criticism, and domain context.

process_signals.name: threat_sensitivity
process_signals.llm_rule: Use to explain anxious or bracing language rather than jumping directly to fear labels.

process_signals.name: perseverative_cognition
process_signals.meaning: Looping, rumination, and mentally stuck processing.
process_signals.llm_rule: Use as a process explanation when distress keeps circling rather than moving.

process_signals.name: behavioral_activation
process_signals.meaning: Approach, doing, initiation, and behavioral movement.
process_signals.llm_rule: Distinguish from reward. A person may act without feeling much pull.

process_signals.name: social_avoidance
process_signals.meaning: Pulling away from contact or reducing social exposure.
process_signals.llm_rule: Do not equate with low social salience; some avoided domains may still be highly organizing.

process_signals.name: relational_ambivalence
process_signals.meaning: Relationship or intimacy movement that feels mixed, misaligned, or farther than wanted.
process_signals.llm_rule: Support summaries like socially active but relationally misaligned.

process_signals.name: social_evaluative_concern
process_signals.meaning: Monitoring how one is seen, judged, or evaluated.
process_signals.llm_rule: Use when performance, embarrassment, attraction, or rejection are central.

process_signals.name: self_criticism
process_signals.meaning: Harsh self-judgment, defectiveness, or shame-oriented language.
process_signals.llm_rule: Distinguish from sadness. This is about stance toward self, not only mood.

process_signals.name: approach_bias
process_signals.meaning: Movement toward reward, people, goals, or contact.
process_signals.llm_rule: Useful for separating activated pursuit from passive positive tone.

process_signals.name: avoidance_bias
process_signals.meaning: Movement away from challenge, discomfort, or contact.
process_signals.llm_rule: Use with social and threat processes, not as a standalone explanation.

process_signals.name: boundary_diffusion
process_signals.llm_rule: Helps explain relational drift, people-pleasing, or weakened agency in relationships.

process_signals.name: negative_audience_effect
process_signals.meaning: Other people impairing focus, reward, or performance.
process_signals.llm_rule: Useful when social presence alters functioning rather than simply mood.

process_signals.name: uncertain_threat_anticipation
process_signals.meaning: Fear building because uncertainty is unresolved.
process_signals.llm_rule: Explain anticipatory strain even before clear adverse events happen.

process_signals.name: agency_awareness
process_signals.meaning: Reflective awareness linked to authorship and intentional response.
process_signals.llm_rule: Use when the person sounds able to notice and redirect rather than only react.

process_signals.name: somatic_burden
process_signals.llm_rule: Keep body-state in view; not all low motivation is purely psychological.

process_signals.name: imagery_density
process_signals.meaning: Concrete scenes, objects, and image-bearing expression.
process_signals.llm_rule: High imagery means the text may be carrying affect through scenes, not only statements.

process_signals.name: sensory_grounding
process_signals.llm_rule: Use to note immediacy and lived quality, not just intensity.

process_signals.name: affective_explicitness
process_signals.llm_rule: High explicitness supports more literal reading of affect words.

process_signals.name: affective_implication
process_signals.meaning: Indirect communication of feeling through imagery or metaphor.
process_signals.llm_rule: High implication means low direct feeling language should not be mistaken for low affect.

process_signals.name: abstract_reflection
process_signals.llm_rule: Use when the person is processing life through pattern, identity, and narrative rather than only event report.

computational_axes.name: dopaminergic_pressure
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate reward drive, incentive salience, and action vigor.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Use to explain pull, spark, or blunted wanting. Do not talk as though dopamine was measured.

computational_axes.name: control_allocation
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate availability and value of control deployment.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Useful when the person knows what to do but cannot hold effort there.

computational_axes.name: volatility_expectancy
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate expectation of instability or abrupt change.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Use for a world-model organized around unpredictability.

computational_axes.name: prediction_error_weighting
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate how hard cues, deviations, or surprises hit.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Useful when small events seem to punch through disproportionately.

computational_axes.name: social_salience
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate how strongly the social channel is organizing the moment.
computational_axes.llm_rule: High salience is not inherently positive; it only means the social field carries weight.

computational_axes.name: effort_cost_load
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate how costly action and self-regulation feel.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Use to explain uphill effort, depletion, and adherence difficulties.

computational_axes.name: social_reward_coupling
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate how strongly reward and performance depend on social context.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Useful when other people seem to set value or disrupt access to reward.

computational_axes.name: threat_hazard_expectancy
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate the feeling that unresolved time itself increases danger.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Use for prolonged waiting, countdown pressure, and escalating unresolved apprehension.

computational_axes.name: agency_coherence
computational_axes.meaning: Approximate coherence of awareness, boundaries, and intentional choice.
computational_axes.llm_rule: Use to explain fragmentation versus authorship without overclaiming identity disturbance.

higher_order_factors.name: negative_affectivity
higher_order_factors.meaning: Broad negative tone, threat, criticism, and distress loading.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Summary factor only. Do not let it erase lower-level nuance.

higher_order_factors.name: internalizing_distress
higher_order_factors.meaning: Broader low-valence, low-reward, self-focused distress configuration.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Use as a broader pattern summary, not a substitute for symptoms.

higher_order_factors.name: internalizing_fear
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Useful when activation and anticipation are dominant.

higher_order_factors.name: detachment
higher_order_factors.meaning: Low reward, low social ease, and flatter disengagement.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Keep distinct from simple introversion or temporary solitude.

higher_order_factors.name: disinhibition
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Use carefully and only when control loss is really part of the state.

higher_order_factors.name: social_anxious_attachment
higher_order_factors.meaning: Social monitoring, relational ambivalence, and interpersonal hyper-attunement.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Useful for relational worry or approval sensitivity.

higher_order_factors.name: interpersonal_instability
higher_order_factors.meaning: Boundary, social-reward, uncertainty, and relationship instability cluster.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Use to summarize unstable relational organization across several interpersonal signals.

higher_order_factors.name: compulsive_rigidity
higher_order_factors.meaning: Perseveration, low flexibility, and rigid control style.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Use when the person sounds stuck, totalizing, and unable to loosen their frame.

higher_order_factors.name: positive_engagement
higher_order_factors.meaning: Protective cluster of reward, connection, flexibility, activation, and positive tone.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Do not overstate this if another domain is simultaneously deteriorating.

higher_order_factors.name: expressive_symbolization
higher_order_factors.meaning: Image-rich, sensory, reflective, and indirect expressive style.
higher_order_factors.llm_rule: Use to explain how the person is communicating, not only what they are feeling.

global_interpretation_rules: Treat current state and trajectory as related but not identical.
Do not collapse conflicting life domains into one flat mood statement.
Use time-scale explicitly when interpreting change.
Respect expressive style as signal, not noise.
Do not diagnose from text alone.
Treat scores as approximations of a person-in-context rather than measurements of isolated symptoms.
